solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Queen is aboard newer boat at sea or on river?

indicators.note: being aboard means sitting inside the vessel, so one piece goes into the other
at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of newer boat are rearranged

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A monarch climbs into a newly built boat out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges NEWERBOAT and 'is aboard' slips R (Regina) into that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carried on a river is transported by water, the question mark flagging a loose example.

clue.text: Friendly email sent about place for advice

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go round the advice office
sent in the sense of sent flying or scattered, so the letters of email are shuffled

parts.note: CAB is the Citizens Advice Bureau, a British free advice service

explanation.surface: A cordial message is sent off to an advice service.
explanation.walkthrough: The Citizens Advice Bureau is a British charity giving free advice; 'sent' rearranges the email's letters as AMILE before the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an amicable person is warm and well disposed, as a friendly one is.

clue.text: Periods oddly unavailable for religious festival

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of periods are not available, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Certain periods are strangely off limits during a holy festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Eid is a Muslim festival, such as the one marking the end of Ramadan.

clue.text: With starter portions of breakfast, have toast

indicators.note: the opening portion of the word breakfast is taken, its first two letters

parts.note: to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: Having a bit of breakfast to begin with, then some toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter portions of' takes the opening pair BR from 'breakfast'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to toast bread is to brown it under heat.

clue.text: PC's sardonic-sounding expression, largely

indicators.note: sounding means the words are judged by how they are heard when spoken

parts.note: sardonic means wry, mocking

indicators.note: largely means most of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an expression in the voice is its tone

explanation.surface: A police constable's mocking turn of phrase, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' looks like a police constable but means politically correct. Spoken together, WRY and TON (most of TONE, by 'largely') make the phrase heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Politically correct and fashionably liberal views are described informally as right-on.

clue.text: Employed by European firm, this person's highly rated

indicators.note: employed by a firm means working within it, so the setter's piece goes inside

parts.note: firm in the sense of steady means stable
this person is means the setter: I am, shortened to I'M

explanation.surface: Someone working for a European company is held in high regard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this person' is the setter speaking of themself, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an estimable person deserves esteem, so is well thought of.

clue.text: Britain has rejected private sort of prison

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the soldier is read backwards

parts.note: a GI is a private soldier in the US army

explanation.surface: Britain has turned down a private kind of jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' is not secret but a soldier, GI.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a ship's prison, also slang for a military lock-up.

clue.text: Illegally disposing of footwear and short trousers

parts.note: a boot is an item of footwear

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: leggings are tight trousers

explanation.surface: Someone is unlawfully getting rid of shoes and cut-down trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the last S from LEGGINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootlegging is making or selling goods, especially alcohol, unlawfully.

clue.text: Imagine current discussion without involvement of Brexiteers' leader

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: without involvement means taking part away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a debate is a formal discussion

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Picture the current argument with the Brexit campaign's figurehead left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes B from 'Brexiteers'' and 'without involvement of' removes it from DEBATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to ideate is to form an idea or picture something in the mind.

clue.text: Good following girls on Twitter

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this letter is placed last

parts.note: birds is British slang for girls

explanation.surface: A nice follower of young women on a social media site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twitter' looks like the social media site but is the twittering sound of birds. BIRDS is British slang for girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds' chirping is called twitter, so birdsong is this, by example.

clue.text: Digger reversing into Isleworth

indicators.note: reversing means the hidden letters are read backwards
into signals that the letters lie inside the place name

explanation.surface: An excavator backs into a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Isleworth is a part of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small garden tool for digging holes.

clue.text: Chopped nuts next to a new drinks dispenser

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: barmy is British slang for crazy, nuts

explanation.surface: Chopped nuts beside a new machine for drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' means mad, not food; 'Chopped' cuts the Y off BARMY.
explanation.definitionFit: A barman serves out drinks in a pub, so is wittily a dispenser of them.

clue.text: Crazy outfit seen on celebrity singer

parts.note: crazy means mad
a rig is an outfit of clothes
an A-list person is a top celebrity

explanation.surface: A wild costume is spotted on a famous vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigalist sings or writes madrigals, part songs for several voices.

clue.text: Agency worker, former model

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker from an agency
late means former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: A temporary office worker who used to be a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a catwalk model but is a pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a template is a pattern to copy, just as a model is.

clue.text: Happy just for men to carry a single black case

parts.note: happy means glad

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the stag piece goes round the others

parts.note: a stag event, such as a stag party, is for men only
a single means one
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Pleased that a men-only grooming product holds one dark case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just for men' reads as a hair-dye brand but is the stag of a stag party. A Gladstone bag is a hinged leather travelling bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gladstone bag is a type of light portmanteau, a travel case named after the prime minister.

clue.text: Eats duck, rejecting initial portion: it's not cooked

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or tampered with, so the letters are mixed up
the opening letter of the word duck is thrown out

explanation.surface: Someone eats a duck, refusing the first slice since it is raw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting initial portion' turns 'duck' into UCK, and 'cooked' rearranges UCK with ITSNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to tuck into food is to eat it heartily.

clue.text: Tex-Mex, say, after cool drink

indicators.note: after means following, so this piece comes second

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
Tex-Mex is an example of fusion cooking, which blends cuisines

explanation.surface: Having Mexican food followed by a cold drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion is a drink made by steeping leaves, such as tea.

clue.text: Where religious person is sheltering knight? That is awkward

indicators.note: sheltering means holding protectively inside

parts.note: a nun lives in a convent
N is the chess notation for knight
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A nun is hiding a knight in her cloister, which is awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheltering' puts N + IE inside IN CONVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something inconvenient causes trouble or is awkward.

clue.text: Geordie wives greeting 70s-style music

parts.note: a Geordie is from Tyneside, in north-east England, so NE
W is an abbreviation for wives, or wife
a wave is a greeting

explanation.surface: Tyneside wives say hello to music of the 1970s.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is someone from Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: New wave was a late 1970s rock genre that followed punk.

clue.text: No end of confusion over island's burial sites

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece
no end means the last letter is taken away

parts.note: a tumult is noisy confusion

explanation.surface: Endless chaos above an island's graveyards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' drops the final T from TUMULT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumuli are ancient mounds of earth heaped over graves.

clue.text: Bird and dog, a small animal

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A list of creatures: a bird, a dog and a little beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A curassow is a large turkey-like bird of tropical America.

clue.text: I travel through place: gorge

indicators.note: travelling through means passing within

parts.note: to place something is to put it
to travel is to go

explanation.surface: A traveller passes through a canyon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gorge' looks like a ravine but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to pig out is to eat greedily, to gorge yourself.

clue.text: Singer's held up gratuity — smallest amount possible?

indicators.note: in a down clue held up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a gratuity is a tip
the stingiest tip would be one penny, written 1p, read as I and P

explanation.surface: A singer has his tip delayed, the meanest amount possible.
explanation.walkthrough: TIP + IP (one penny, 1p) is read backwards, held up being reversal in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipit is a small songbird, so a singer by example.

clue.text: Topping with cake rejected by North African

indicators.note: by means next to, placing the letter after
rejected means sent back, so read backwards

parts.note: topping is old British slang for excellent, A1, written AI
a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: A North African turns down a cake with icing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' is not icing but old slang for excellent, A1. 'North' is not part of the definition but gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nubian comes from Nubia, a region of north-east Africa.

clue.text: Reading matter a writer put on page ten in Le Monde

indicators.note: put on means placed next to, so the writer follows the page

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
dix is French for ten; Le Monde is a French newspaper

explanation.surface: A journalist places a story on page ten of a French newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix is extra material at the back of a book, matter to be read.

clue.text: Sounds like score's nil

indicators.note: sounds like means the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to score is to nick, mark with a cut, so score's gives nicks

explanation.surface: It sounds as though the match score is nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: nix means nothing at all.

clue.text: Brand new home overshadowed by mountain

indicators.note: overshadowed means covered, so the home piece sits inside the peak

parts.note: MT is the abbreviation for mount or mountain
in means at home

explanation.surface: A newly built house in the shadow of a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: In mint condition means as good as new, unused.

clue.text: Making public cuts, as it were, is burdensome

parts.note: overt means open, public
axing is cutting, as of jobs or spending

explanation.surface: Announcing spending cuts is a heavy burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it were' signals reading the answer split in two, a public cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtaxing means putting too great a strain on, so making it a burden.
